 On The 3 rd Of September, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 8832 of 2024
 Ajay Sondhiya
 Versus
Samayak Sinh Chauhan And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Harshit Pandey - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Gulab Chand Sohane, learned counsel for the respon
 Order
The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 03.09.2024, passed in MACC No.13/2022 by 5th Additional MACT, Jabalpur.
By the said award, learned Tribunal has partly allowed the claim case and awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.75,350/- along with the interest of 6% per annum.
2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 26.07.2021, appellant aged about 39 years was going to his home on his TVS motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-20-NK-8572.

When he reached near Yadgar Chowk at around 8:45 P.M., one grey colored Maruti Swift Car bearing engine No.K12NP1077281 and chassis No.MBHCZCB35MF822972 coming from tope tiraha side being driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner dashed claimant from front, due to which appellant claimant fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury on occipital bone and various other parts of the body.
He remained in hospital for around 15 days.

3. Learned Claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:42311 2 MA-8832-2024 rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1.
The offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance Company on the fateful day.
The appellant /claimant filed a claim petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.

4. Learned MACT awarded Rs.25,000/- under the head of "medical expenses", Rs.3,000/- under the head "Transportation", Rs.4350/- under the head of "loss of income due to accident", Rs.3,000/- for "attender" and Rs.5,000/- for "special diet" under pecuniary head and under non- pecuniary heads MACT awarded Rs.25,000/- for grievous injuries and Rs. 10,000/- for pain and suffering.
Thus in total, learned MACT awarded Rs.75,350/- as against Rs.10,00,000/-.

sentences.text: 5. It is not in dispute that respondent was responsible for causing the accident.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?.
6. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. After going through the record and hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I find that Tribunal has awarded lower side amount under various heads which is modified and recalculated in the table below for ready reference:
 Head Before Modified  Medical Expenses Rs.25,000/- Rs.75,000/-
 Transportation Rs.3,000/- Rs.15,000/-
Loss of income due to accident Rs.4350/- Rs.8,000/-
 Attender Rs.3,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 Special Diet Rs.5,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 Grievous injury Rs.25,000/- Rs.50,000/-
 Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/- Rs.50,000/-
 Total Rs.75,350/- Rs.1,78,000/-
 After deduction Rs.1,78,000/-
 -75,350/-
 Rs.1,02,650/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42311  3   8 .
Considering the overall facts and circumsta appellant is entitled for enhancement for a sum of Rs.1,02,650/- which shall also carry same interest as has been awarded by the Tribunal.

9. In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference and the compensation amount is liable to be and is hereby enhanced from Rs.75,350/- to Rs.1,78,000/-.

Thus after deduction the enhanced amount comes to Rs.1,02,650/- which shall be payable along with interest 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization against the respondent No.1 to 3/non-applicants jointly and severally.

"i. The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
